The former part no doubt contains the right view; the following verse proves it, “Overcome evil with good.” The idea of “heaping coals of fire” is said to have been derived from the practice of heaping coals on the fire to melt hard metals; but as “the coals of fire” must mean “burning coals,” as indeed the word in <reference osisRef="Bible:Prov.25.22">Proverbs 25:22</reference>, whence the passage is taken, clearly means, this notion cannot be entertained. It seems to be a sort of proverbial saying, signifying something intolerable, which cannot be borne without producing strong effects: such is represented to be kindness to any enemy, to feed him when hungry and to give him drink when thirsty, has commonly such a power over him that he cannot resist its influence, no more than he can withstand the scorching heat of burning coals. Of course the natural tendency of such a conduct is all that is intended, and not that it invariably produces such an effect; for in Scripture things are often stated in this way; but human nature is such a strange thing, that it often resists what is right, just, and reasonable, and reverses, as it were, the very nature of things.<div eID="gen115530" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen115531" type="x-p"/>It is not true what <name>Whitby</name> and others have held, that “coals of fire” always mean judgments or punishments. The word indeed in certain connections, as in <reference osisRef="Bible:Ps.18.13 Bible:Ps.140.10">Psalm 18:13; Psalm 140:10</reference>, has this meaning, but in <reference osisRef="Bible:Prov.25.22">Proverbs 25:22</reference>, it cannot be taken in this sense, as the preceding verse most clearly proves. There is no canon of interpretation more erroneous than to make words or phrases to bear the same meaning in every place. — <hi type="italic">Ed.</hi><div eID="gen115531" type="x-p"/> </note><div eID="gen115529" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Rom.12.20" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen115527" osisID="Rom.12.20" type="section"/>
entries.7b4f117613f1526b659220ba917f85fcc17f85a8:
21. Be not overcome by evil, etc. This sentence is laid down as a confirmation; for in this case our contest is altogether with perverseness, if we try to retaliate it, we confess that we are overcome by it; if, on the contrary, we return good for evil, by that very deed we show the invincible firmness of our mind. This is truly a most glorious kind of victory, the fruit of which is not only apprehended by the mind, but really perceived, while the Lord is giving success to their patience, than which they can wish nothing better. On the other hand, he who attempts to overcome evil with evil, may perhaps surpass his enemy in doing injury, but it is to his own ruin; for by acting thus he carries on war for the devil.
CHAPTER 13
Romans 13:1-2
1. Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.
1. Omnis anima potestatibus supereminentibus subdita sit: non enim est potestas, nisi a Deo; quae vero sunt potestates a Deo sunt ordinatae.
2. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.
2. Itaque qui resistit potestati, Dei ordinationi resistit; qui vero restiterint judicium sibi accersent.

entries.d37d7cb95bce7fd04ac71cbf1d17b2a7f958ca8f:

               <ns0:head>CHAP. XII.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1. <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Hitherto the Apostle hath Discoursed of matters of <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi>; in this, and the following Chapters, he sets down precepts of <ns0:hi>Holy Life.</ns0:hi> He useth the word in the <ns0:hi>plural</ns0:hi> number, to amplifie and set forth the manifold <ns0:hi>Mercies of God,</ns0:hi> in Election, Justification, Adoption, <ns0:hi>&c. q. d.</ns0:hi> See<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing you <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> have received so many, and so great <ns0:hi>Mercies</ns0:hi> from God; seeing he hath preferred you to his <ns0:hi>Ancient People the Iewes,</ns0:hi> and hath chosen and called you, when he hath rejected them; as you value these <ns0:hi>Mercies,</ns0:hi> let the consideration of them engage you to all manner of <ns0:hi>Holiness and New Obedience.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> I <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>I exhort you.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="‖" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>well plea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God <ns0:hi>b,</ns0:hi> that ye <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 6.13.16.</ns0:note> pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">That you Give, Dedicate and Offer up, as <ns0:hi>Spiritual Priests,</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> your bodies <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Your selves, or your whole man, a part is put for the whole; the body is named, because it is the Souls Instrument in the service of God.</ns0:note> a living sacrifice <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Sacrifices</ns0:hi> of Old were <ns0:hi>Presented alive to God,</ns0:hi> and their Blood was shed at the Feet of the <ns0:hi>Altar:</ns0:hi> A Beast that dyed of its self, or was Torn by wild Beasts, was not to be <ns0:hi>Sacrificed:</ns0:hi> Nay, it was not so much as to be eaten, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 22.31. <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 22.8. Conformable here<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />unto, God will have us <ns0:hi>Offer up our selves a living Sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fice, i. e.</ns0:hi> We must be quickned and Alive to God, and not Dead in Sins and Trespasses.</ns0:note>, holy <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">As the Sacrifices un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der the Law, were to be without <ns0:hi>blemish or defect, Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.5. <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 1.10. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 15.21.</ns0:note>, acceptable unto God <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Or well pleasing unto God. So were the appointed <ns0:hi>Sacrifices</ns0:hi> under the <ns0:hi>Law, Levit.</ns0:hi> 1.9, So was the <ns0:hi>Sacrifice of Christ the Lamb of God, Eph.</ns0:hi> 5.2. and so are all <ns0:hi>Spiritual Sacrifices under the Gospel, Phil.</ns0:hi> 4.18. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 13.16.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>which is</ns0:hi> your reasonable service <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Or which is a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />greeable to Reason; Nothing is more Reasonable, than that you should Devote your selves to God in this man<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ner. Some think this is added, To shew a difference be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tween the <ns0:hi>Sacrifice</ns0:hi> here required, and that of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> which was of unreasonable Beasts. Others, by <ns0:hi>reasonable service,</ns0:hi> understand <ns0:hi>spiritual Service,</ns0:hi> and Expound this place by 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.5. where you read of <ns0:hi>Spiritual Sacrifices ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceptable to</ns0:hi> God <ns0:hi>by Iesus Christ.</ns0:hi> Others think, That by <ns0:hi>reasonable,</ns0:hi> you must understand such <ns0:hi>Service,</ns0:hi> as is accor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding to the <ns0:hi>Word of God</ns0:hi>; and this Suits best with the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> Phrase in the Text. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. The same word is used, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.2. and there 'tis rendred the <ns0:hi>Milk</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Word,</ns0:hi> and not reasonable <ns0:hi>Milk.</ns0:hi> And so the <ns0:hi>Service</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Worship</ns0:hi> here spoken of, is oppos'd to that <ns0:hi>Will-worship,</ns0:hi> of which you read in <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 2.23.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2. And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 2.15.</ns0:note> be not conformed to this <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>to this <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> world <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Do not Fashion or Accommodate your selves to the cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rupt Principles, Customes, or Courses of worldly and wicked Men; and what they are, you will find in <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 13.13. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 5.18, 19. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 4.3. You have somewhat the like Counsel, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 23.2. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.14.</ns0:note>: but be ye <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>altered in form and fashion: Metamor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phosed.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Eph. 1.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Col. 1.21, 22. and 3.10.</ns0:note> transformed by the renewing of your mind <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> Be you Regenerated, and changed in your Whole Man; be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ginning at the Mind, by which the <ns0:hi>Spirit of God worketh</ns0:hi> upon the inferior Faculties of the Soul, <ns0:hi>vid. Eph.</ns0:hi> 4.23.</ns0:note>, that ye may <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Thes. 4.3.</ns0:note> prove what <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> that good, and acceptable and perfect will of God <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">By <ns0:hi>proving,</ns0:hi> understand <ns0:hi>Discerning</ns0:hi>: By the <ns0:hi>Will of God,</ns0:hi> His <ns0:hi>revealed Will</ns0:hi> in his Word; and so it best Accords with the <ns0:hi>reasonable Service</ns0:hi> spoken of, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 1. and with the Scope of the Text it self; which is, to exhort unto <ns0:hi>holiness</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>obedience,</ns0:hi> which is according to the <ns0:hi>Rule</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Word.</ns0:hi> He annexeth <ns0:hi>Three Adjuncts</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Will</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Word of God; It is good</ns0:hi>; Revealed only for our Benefit. It is <ns0:hi>Accepta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble, i. e.</ns0:hi> By Obedience thereunto we shall be Accepted: It is <ns0:hi>Perfect,</ns0:hi> and the Observance thereof will make us <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o too, 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 3.17. There are different Readings of these Words, but all to the same Sence. Some thus, That you may <ns0:hi>prove</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Will of God,</ns0:hi> which to do, is <ns0:hi>Good, Accep<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />table,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Perfect.</ns0:hi> Others thus, <ns0:hi>That you may prove what the Will of God is</ns0:hi>; and <ns0:hi>what is good, acceptable,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fect.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3. <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Before he Exhorted to a Holy Life in general, now he comes to more particular Exhortations.</ns0:note> For I say <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> I En<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />joyn and Command, <ns0:hi>vid. Gal.</ns0:hi> 5.16. <ns0:hi>I</ns0:hi> do not only <ns0:hi>be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />seech you,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 1. but I also Require you as one that hath Authority.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 3.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> through the grace given unto me <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">See on <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 1.5.</ns0:note>, to every man that is among you <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">More particularly to him, that hath any particular Gift or Office in the Church.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Prov. 25.27. Eccl. 7.16.</ns0:note> not to think <ns0:hi>of himself</ns0:hi> more highly than he ought to think <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Not to be Drunk with a proud and overweening Conceit of himself; his own <ns0:hi>Wisdom, Ability,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note>; but to <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>to be <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> to sobriety.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> think soberly <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Or <ns0:hi>Modestly,</ns0:hi> let him contain himself within Bounds, and not take upon him what doth not belong to him; let him not Contemn others, and pretend to more than he hath. There is an elegant Paranomosia in the <ns0:hi>Greek,</ns0:hi> which our Language cannot reach.</ns0:note> ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 12.7, 11.</ns0:note> as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> here is put for the <ns0:hi>Knowledge of God</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi>; and all other <ns0:hi>spiritual gifts</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>graces</ns0:hi> bestowed upon the <ns0:hi>Faithful:</ns0:hi> These are called <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> because they are given with <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> and exercised by <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi>; of these, God deals to every Man his <ns0:hi>measure</ns0:hi> or Portion: Not <ns0:hi>all gifts</ns0:hi> to one, nor the same <ns0:hi>gift</ns0:hi> to every one in the same <ns0:hi>measure</ns0:hi> or proportion, <ns0:hi>vid. ver.</ns0:hi> 6. and <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 4.7.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4. For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 12.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Eph. 4.16.</ns0:note> as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fice;</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5. So <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 10.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> we being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">These Verses are a Reason against Arrogancy. All Christians are <ns0:hi>members</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>same Body</ns0:hi>; there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore, they should not Pride themselves in their <ns0:hi>gifts,</ns0:hi> but employ them for the Common Good. It is with the Church, the <ns0:hi>Mystical body of Christ,</ns0:hi> as with a natural <ns0:hi>body</ns0:hi> that hath many <ns0:hi>members, and all these have not the same Office,</ns0:hi> or the same Action or Operation (as the word signifieth) The Eye hath one <ns0:hi>Office,</ns0:hi> the Ear another, the Hand a third, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> So the <ns0:hi>Church of Christ,</ns0:hi> though one <ns0:hi>body</ns0:hi> in him who is the <ns0:hi>Head,</ns0:hi> hath many <ns0:hi>Members</ns0:hi>; ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny in regard of their Persons, and many in regard of their <ns0:hi>Offices,</ns0:hi> which are various and diverse; and which is more, The <ns0:hi>members</ns0:hi> are every one <ns0:hi>members</ns0:hi> one of ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther. <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> They are joynt and fellow <ns0:hi>Members</ns0:hi>; as they have a common Relation to the same <ns0:hi>Head,</ns0:hi> so a mutual Relation to one another. Therefore Christians, especi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally <ns0:hi>Church-Officers,</ns0:hi> should not contemn one another, or intrude upon the <ns0:hi>Office</ns0:hi> of each other; but all should use their Gifts to the Good and Edification of others.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:427" />6. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 12.4. 1 Pet. 4.10, 11.</ns0:note> Having then gifts, differing according to the grace that is given to us <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Or seeing we have different <ns0:hi>gifts</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>offices,</ns0:hi> accor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding as the <ns0:hi>grace of God</ns0:hi> hath bestowed them upon us, let us use them Aright. This is added to prevent Pride and Envy: None should be <ns0:hi>proud</ns0:hi> of that he hath him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self, or <ns0:hi>envy</ns0:hi> what another hath, seeing all is of <ns0:hi>Grace.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, whether <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 12.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, 28. & 13.2. & 14.1, 29, 31.</ns0:note> prophesy, <ns0:hi>let us prophesy</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">These words, <ns0:hi>Let us Prophesy,</ns0:hi> are not in the Text; but they are put in by our Translators, to fill up the Sence. There is an Ellipsis in the Words, and something must be inserted. Some make the Supply from the last words in the foregoing Verse, <ns0:hi>Let us be one anothers Members</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Prophesying,</ns0:hi> Teaching, Exhorting, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Others think, it ought to be supplyed out of <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> Whether we have <ns0:hi>Prophesy,</ns0:hi> let us be <ns0:hi>wise</ns0:hi> unto <ns0:hi>sobriety</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Prophesying</ns0:hi>; and so in all the rest that follow: In all the several <ns0:hi>gifts</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>offices,</ns0:hi> he sheweth how they should behave themselves. The <ns0:hi>Greek Scholiast,</ns0:hi> will have supply'd in them all (<ns0:hi>let us persevere.</ns0:hi>) By <ns0:hi>Prophesying,</ns0:hi> in this place, you may un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstand an extraordinary <ns0:hi>Gift,</ns0:hi> that some had in Under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />standing <ns0:hi>divine Mysteries,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Old-Testament Prophesies,</ns0:hi> with a wonderful Dexterity in applying the same; to which was joyned, sometimes the Revelation of Secret, and Future things, <ns0:hi>vid. Act.</ns0:hi> 11.27. and 21.9.</ns0:note> according to the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />portion of faith <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> They that have this <ns0:hi>gift of Prophesying,</ns0:hi> must exercise it accor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ding to the <ns0:hi>measure of Knowledge,</ns0:hi> in heavenly <ns0:hi>mysteries,</ns0:hi> that God hath given them: Or else, in their <ns0:hi>Prophesy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing,</ns0:hi> they must have regard to the Articles of <ns0:hi>Christian Faith,</ns0:hi> and see that they regulate themselves according thereunto. Some think, he calls the Holy Scripture in general, an Analogy or Proportion of <ns0:hi>faith</ns0:hi>; by these, the false Prophets of Old, were discerned, if they delive<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red any thing contrary thereunto (<ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 13.1. &c.) Others think, he speaks of certain Principles, or Heads of Christi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />an Religion (<ns0:hi>vid. Heb.</ns0:hi> 6.1.) from which the Prophets and others, were not to swerve; Yea, some think, he aimes at the Symbol and Creed, called the Apostles; which, from the Beginning, was called the <ns0:hi>Analogy of Faith.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7. Or ministry <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Under this Word, are comprehended, all ordinary Ec<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clesiastical Functions, which afterwards divideth into two Sorts: The <ns0:hi>First</ns0:hi> relating to the <ns0:hi>Word</ns0:hi>; The <ns0:hi>Second</ns0:hi> to other <ns0:hi>pious Works.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>let us wait</ns0:hi> on <ns0:hi>our</ns0:hi> ministring <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">These words <ns0:hi>(Let us wait)</ns0:hi> are not in the Text, but fitly supplyed. <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> Let all that be called to the <ns0:hi>office</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Ministry,</ns0:hi> be diligent in it, and attend to it, <ns0:hi>vid. Act.</ns0:hi> 20.28. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 5.2.</ns0:note>; or he that teacheth, on teaching <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Teaching,</ns0:hi> in the latter end of this Verse; and <ns0:hi>Exhorting,</ns0:hi> in the be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ginning of the next, are mentioned, as the Two great <ns0:hi>Works</ns0:hi> of those, that <ns0:hi>minister</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>labour</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Word</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Doctrine:</ns0:hi> Some think, they are distinct <ns0:hi>Offices; (vid. Eph.</ns0:hi> 4.11.) and that in the <ns0:hi>primitive Church,</ns0:hi> where they had variety of <ns0:hi>Ministers</ns0:hi>; some had the <ns0:hi>office</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Teachers,</ns0:hi> and chiefly exercised themselves in Instructing their <ns0:hi>Hearers</ns0:hi> in the Principles of Religion; in laying down sound Doc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trine, and Confuting of Errors. Others had the <ns0:hi>office</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Pastors,</ns0:hi> and attended chiefly to Exhortation and Admoni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion; pressing Points of Practise, and making Application thereof. Others think, that they are distinct <ns0:hi>gifts,</ns0:hi> but not divers <ns0:hi>offices</ns0:hi>; some have a <ns0:hi>gift</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Teach,</ns0:hi> that have none to Exhort and <ns0:hi>è Contra.</ns0:hi> The Apostle, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 6. calls them differing <ns0:hi>gifts</ns0:hi>; sometimes these Two are found in the same Persons, and they are excellently Gifted, both for <ns0:hi>Teaching</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Exhorting.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8. Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">See the Notes on the foregoing Verse.</ns0:note>: he <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 6.1, 2, 3.</ns0:note> that <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> giveth, <ns0:hi>let him do it</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>liberality.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> with sim<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plicity <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> He that hath the <ns0:hi>office</ns0:hi> of Collecting and Distributing the <ns0:hi>Church-Almes</ns0:hi> (which was the <ns0:hi>Deacons</ns0:hi> Work or Charge, <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 6.1. &c.) <ns0:hi>Let him</ns0:hi> discharge <ns0:hi>it with simplicity,</ns0:hi> or with <ns0:hi>singleness of Heart.</ns0:hi> (So the word is rendred, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 6.5.) Let him do it Faithfully and Impartially, and without Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vour or Affection.</ns0:note>; he that ruleth <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Or he that is a President, and set over others. There is great difference amongst <ns0:hi>Exposi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tors,</ns0:hi> who is meant by this Ruler. It is not meant of State-Rulers (of them he Treats in the next Chapter) but of <ns0:hi>Church-Rulers.</ns0:hi> Some understand, all <ns0:hi>Church-Officers</ns0:hi> in general.                      <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Either make him relent, or bring down the greater Vengeance from God upon him. This is taken out of <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 25.21, 22. See the Notes there.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21. Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">This Verse is a divine Aphorisme: therein the Apostle Anticipates an objection. Some might be ready to say, if we should follow this Advice we should be counted Cowards and Dastards, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> To this he Answers, That tis the ready way to be Triumphers and Conquerors. By <ns0:hi>evil,</ns0:hi> here, he means, the <ns0:hi>wrongs</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>injuries</ns0:hi> of men; and to be <ns0:hi>overcome</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>evil,</ns0:hi> is to be mov'd and provoked there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />by to Impatience or Malice. When tis thus with a Man, he is overcome, or conquered: in <ns0:hi>revenge</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>injuries,</ns0:hi> he is a loser that gets the better. Therefore he Exhorts us, rather to <ns0:hi>overcome evil with good,</ns0:hi> that is a Noble Victo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry indeed: This is the way not to be Even with him that <ns0:hi>wrongs</ns0:hi> us, but to be Above him. Thus <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> overcame <ns0:hi>Saul,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Elisha</ns0:hi> the Bands of <ns0:hi>Syria.</ns0:hi> This is the way to <ns0:hi>overcome</ns0:hi> our selves, and our Adversaries too; Our selves, in denying our lusts that egge us on to Revenge; our Adversaries, in winning them to relent and acknow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge their miscarriages.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
